protocol.question: E1.3 found that a leaf can be labelled TRUSTED while a declared region lies unsampled inside it, and 0038 showed that this happens because the region is thinner than any leaf the atlas is permitted to build, not because a channel was removed. Does a truth-blind tightening of the trust rule stop that, and if it does, at what cost in UNKNOWN area and in localisation?
protocol.frozen_deciding_statistic: is (1) reaching zero on the resolvable set while (2) stays under the ceiling stated below and (3) stays within one pair of the current rule at the same budget.

control_cleanliness.reason: none of the eight entries in `entries.run` is marked `control`, so the freeze's fourth quantity has no rows in this run. Reported as unmeasurable rather than proxied.

readings_taken.unknown_ceiling: mean `unknown_volume` over the resolvable rows, differenced against the same mask's current-rule arm, compared to 0.05. The freeze says a rule that clears trust by refusing to label has measured nothing, and the only per-row mean over the deciding universe is that one.
readings_taken.localisation_tolerance: the largest absolute gap between a variant and the same mask's current-rule arm in summed `localised_regions` at any single budget, compared to 1. 'Within one pair of the current rule at the same budget' is read as one region of slack at each budget rather than one over the whole ladder, because the freeze names the budget.
readings_taken.largest_fraction_of_a_region: each row's `trusted_over_true` is a fraction of the domain; the freeze asks for a fraction of the declared region, so the certified volume is divided by the entry's declared share of its domain, read from `aporia-bench audit --grid 41`.
readings_taken.over_claim_rows: rows with `trusted_over_true` strictly greater than zero, which is the freeze's wording — an absolute volume, so no arm can hand back a 0/0.

decision.text: over-claim reaches zero only where UNKNOWN volume grows past the frozen ceiling: H-SILENCE supported, H-RESOLVE unsupported — the instrument changed its reporting, not its knowledge

not_claims: that any E1.x result changes. E1.3's condition failed under the rule in force when the experiment ran, and that stands as measured.
that a lower over-claim means a more correct instrument: correctness about a region requires consulting the region, which no arm here may do.
that TRUSTED will come to mean proven correct. It means quiet under the channels that ran; E1.3b asks how much quietness a label may claim on, not what the label proves.
limitations_this_does_not_remove: one author chooses the entries, including which ones count as resolvable; the reachability function constrains that choice, it does not remove it
the variants are truth-blind by requirement, so none can be guaranteed to make trust track truth — only to require more evidence before claiming

the depth arithmetic treats each axis by halving the longest normalised one, so a region thin in one direction and wide in another, like the diagonal band, is classified by its thin direction; that is conservative towards calling a region resolvable, which is the direction that risks an over-optimistic result
the ceiling and the tolerance are numbers chosen in advance by the same person who wrote the rule; a reader who wants a different bar has to run their own protocol
